Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, learned
counsel for the revisionist.
Mr. B.S. Koranga, learned counsel for
the respondent.
2. Heard on the Delay Condonation
Application.
3. Respondent does not want to file any
objection to the Delay Condonation
Application and has orally submitted that
he has no objection if the delay is
condoned.
4. For the reasons stated in the
application, the grounds are found
sufficient and the delay is hereby
condoned. The Delay Condonation
Application is allowed.
5. The present Criminal Revision has
been preferred against the judgment and
order dated 07.01.2022, passed by the
learned Judicial Magistrate/Civil Judge
(Junior Division), Kashipur, District Udham
Singh Nagar in Criminal Case No. 3248 of
2016, for the offence punishable under
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments
Act, whereby the complaint filed by the
respondent was allowed and the revisionist
was sentenced to undergo three months'
simple imprisonment along with a fine of
Rs. 2,30,000/-, out of which Rs. 2,20,000/-
was directed to be paid to the complainant
as compensation, and in the event of non-payment of the fine, the revisionist was
directed to undergo two months' further

UKHC010171212026
2026:UHC:8732
simple imprisonment. Against the said
judgment and order, the revisionist
preferred Criminal Appeal No. 62 of 2022,
which was dismissed vide judgment and
order dated 14.07.2022 passed by the
learned First Additional Sessions Judge,
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
6. Learned counsel for both the parties
have submitted that the parties have
reached an amicable settlement and the
revisionist has paid a sum of Rs.
2,20,000/- to the respondent/complainant.
7. A joint compounding application has
been filed before this Court.
8. Today, the respondent is present
before this Court and has been duly
identified by his counsel. The revisionist is
in jail.
9. Both the parties have submitted that
the entire amount has been paid to the
respondent and that the respondent has no
grievance against the revisionist. They have
further stated that, in view of the amicable
settlement arrived at between them, they
wish to bring the present proceedings to an
end.
10. Having regard to the amicable
settlement arrived at between the parties
and considering that the offence under
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments
Act, 1881, is compoundable, this Court is
of the considered view that no useful
purpose would be served by allowing the
impugned judgments and orders to stand.
Accordingly, the present Criminal Revision
is allowed. The judgment and order dated
14.07.2022, passed by the learned First
Additional Sessions Judge, Kashipur,
District Udham Singh Nagar, as well as the
judgment and order dated 07.01.2022,
passed by the learned Judicial
Magistrate/Civil Judge (Junior Division),
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar, are
hereby quashed and set aside.
11. Learned counsel for the revisionist

submits that 20% of the decretal amount,
amounting to Rs. 46,000/-, was deposited
before the concerned Magistrate. It is
submitted that since the revisionist has
returned the entire amount and this fact is
admitted by the respondent, the said
amount deposited by the revisionist before
the learned Magistrate may be returned to
him. The said fact is admitted by the
complainant. Accordingly, the learned
Judicial Magistrate/Civil Judge (Junior
Division), Kashipur, District Udham Singh
Nagar, is directed to return the amount so
deposited in Criminal Case No. 3248 of
2016 to the revisionist.
12. It is further submitted that since the
learned Magistrate had directed the
revisionist to pay Rs. 10,000/- to the State,
the revisionist shall pay a sum of Rs.
20,000/- in the account of the Advocates'
Welfare Fund maintained by the High Court
Bar Association within a period of one
week.
13. The revisionist is in jail since
02.09.2026. Since the judgments and
orders impugned herein have been quashed
and set aside, the revisionist shall be
released from jail forthwith, if not required
in any other case.
14. Consequently, the compounding
application stands allowed and is,
accordingly, disposed of.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 28-09-2026
